sections.title: Identification and habitat
sections.text: This catalogue entry represents Leucanthemum vulgare, oxeye daisy, rather than the whole genus. A rhizomatous perennial native to Europe, it grows in meadows and disturbed places and is naturalised elsewhere.

sections.title: Size and flower heads
sections.text: The plant is usually 10–30 cm tall but can exceed 1 m. Its flower heads have white ray florets around a yellow disc. Basal leaves are spatulate and toothed or lobed; stem leaves are narrower.

sections.title: Edibility and cautions
sections.text: The leaves are eaten in moderate amounts according to a university horticultural source. Contact with leaves or flowers can cause dermatitis. The oxeye daisy group includes close relatives; identify the plant precisely before any use.
